title: Align institutional stakeholders across all three tiers

blocks.text: The second enabling theme covers who decides and how the plan is run. It holds five focus areas, the most of any theme. They are three-tier alignment, industry collaboration, data and policy, the national deficits moved in from Pillar 2 and workforce skills, which was added in October and flagged as untested.
Theme 3.2 · Governance and leadership · Focus area 16
Align institutional stakeholders across all three tiers

Air service agreements and visas sit with national government, mandates are split across three tiers and the national marketing body is under strain, so the province needs one shared agenda with clear decision rights.

**December 2025.** Review Institutional Arrangements (Wesgro, DEDAT, CTT) (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64), reprinted from March 2026 as Review Institutional Arrangements (local, provincial and national).

**October 2026: Reworded.** Air rights and visas sit nationally. The review of three named bodies widened to alignment across national, provincial and local government. The stakeholder evidence on bilateral agreements and split mandates, the Diagnostic's tier table and MIDAS's account of route designation drove the change.

blocks.caption: The levers the growth case needs are spread across three tiers, and the bodies that hold them are thin or out of step.
blocks.source: Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025 (Diag); Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026 (SIR; statements attributed to organisations, not quotations); MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026; Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026 (IR). The only national government bodies with an appendix table in the first phase of engagement, Stats SA and the Department of Tourism, speak to data alone; SA Tourism has none.
rows: National holds air rights and visas
The national tier holds visa rules and border compliance, and air service agreements and route rights; the province holds jobs, safety programmes and infrastructure planning
Restrictive bilateral air agreements limit airlift and leave the province less competitive than peers (Department of Economic Development)
Chinese routes follow government-to-government agreements, and the designated airline may learn of its designation late
Tourism institutional capacity has eroded at provincial and municipal level over a decade; SA Tourism's weakness constrains otherwise sound international strategies
Mobility responsibilities are split across three tiers; a district, local and LTO mandate disconnect leaves tourism development without a clear owner
ACSA's runway (R6.39bn, about 2033), Transnet's port plans and PRASA's R21.1bn rail programme all sit with national SOEs

blocks.text: What is needed, in the Diagnostic's own words, is a shared growth agenda with clear decision rights and joint delivery plans (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p58). No deliverable maps decision rights by tier beyond that one slide. The national view on air rights, visas and marketing is inferred from provincial and local voices, not heard directly. The two national bodies with appendix tables, Stats SA and the Department of Tourism, spoke only to data, and SA Tourism is listed as engaged with no table (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p16, p30, p37).

Wesgro should convene the shared agenda and hold the evidence the national tier needs, rather than try to own levers it cannot. A Tourism Growth Steerco at Wesgro CEO level, with DEDAT and Cape Town Tourism, gives the province one voice and one route to national decisions (section 4.7). MIDAS shows the route work this needs: early relationships with Indian carriers and the Indian authorities, and with China's state-owned carriers through the government-to-government process (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, Indian and Chinese Market Opportunity).

rows: Constitute the Tourism Growth Steerco, co-chaired with DEDAT and with Cape Town Tourism as a standing member, and agree a decision-rights map by tier from the Diagnostic's tier table
Wesgro CEO's office; DEDAT; Cape Town Tourism
Hold standing relationships with Indian carriers and authorities, with China Southern and China Eastern and with Riyadh Air
Track the national capital programmes that bind the plan (runway, ports and rail) and report on them each quarter
Settle district, local and LTO mandates, restore a tourism development function where it has lapsed and revisit the Discover Garden Route partnership
Test a dedicated transport authority model for tourism-enabling mobility
Agree with the province how marketing and data roles divide between national and provincial bodies

blocks.text: Where the benchmark names the body that negotiates air service agreements, it is national: Chile's civil aviation board and Singapore's aviation authority (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p23, p38). Valencia embeds municipal, provincial and regional authorities in one decision-making system led by Visit València, and the required change for the Western Cape is to embed tourism governance in permanent public-private structures (p47, p49).

**Initiative I15**, Tourism Growth Steerco and three-tier alignment, carries this entry with focus area 17 (section 4.3). **Indicator** T2-21 escalation items answered by the national tier at outcome level (section 5.2).
